solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Man in suit lifting equipment

definitions.meaning: a picture card in a suit of playing cards, ranking below the queen
a device for raising a car to change a wheel

explanation.surface: A man in a business suit is operating some lifting gear.
explanation.definitionFit: The knave is the court card in each suit, and the same word names the car-raising tool used for a flat tyre.

clue.text: Current setter involved in predicament

indicators.note: the jumbled word sits within the predicament

parts.note: to be in a jam is to be in a predicament

indicators.note: involved means tangled or convoluted, so the letters of setter get mixed up

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler finds himself caught up in difficulties at present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' looks like the compiler (ME), but here 'involved' scrambles the word itself; 'in' then places it inside the predicament.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet stream is a fast, narrow current of air high in the atmosphere.

clue.text: V-sign from revolutionary facing little man

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
V stands for versus, against, facing an opponent
Ron is a short form of the man's name Ronald

explanation.surface: A revolutionary makes a rude gesture at a small man.
explanation.walkthrough: V, short for versus, is facing someone in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A chevron is a V-shaped stripe, as on a sergeant's sleeve or a road sign.

clue.text: Something essential to dignitary in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the words to and dignitary are read backwards

parts.note: a VIP is a very important person

explanation.surface: Something vital to an important figure once retired, like a pension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retirement' reverses both words together, the little word 'to' included, which is easy to treat as a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A pivot is the central point on which things turn, hence anything crucial or central.

clue.text: Checked text in page of scripture covered by course

indicators.note: being covered by something means being enclosed by it, so the words go inside the course

parts.note: a road is a course or route
RE is religious education, scripture lessons at school

explanation.surface: An editor checked a passage from the Bible studied on a course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is not a link word here: it goes into the course along with scripture under 'covered by'. RE is school shorthand for religious education.
explanation.definitionFit: To proofread is to examine a draft for errors before printing.

clue.text: Vessel with another following current coming to holy residence

indicators.note: one thing following another comes after it, so the second vessel comes after the current

parts.note: a vat is a large tank or vessel
I is the symbol for electric current
another vessel: a can is a container

explanation.surface: Two boats travel with the current on the way to a holy residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming to' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vatican in Rome is the official residence of the Pope.

clue.text: Electrical engineer beginning to search in web

indicators.note: the first letter goes in the web

parts.note: tela is an anatomical term for a web-like membrane, from the Latin for web

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An engineer starts looking for something online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'web' looks like the internet; it is TELA, a weblike tissue.
explanation.definitionFit: Nikola Tesla was a pioneering inventor in electricity, known for alternating current.

clue.text: Fruit reduced by penny when sold alone

indicators.note: to be reduced by something is to have it subtracted, so the penny is taken from the fruit

parts.note: a peach is a fruit

explanation.surface: A greengrocer cuts the price of fruit by a penny when it is sold singly.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop prices quoted per item, apples at 30p apiece, use this word for goods sold singly.

clue.text: Language operates incoherently without noun

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the jumbled letters are placed outside the noun
incoherently means in a muddled way, so the letters of operates are rearranged

parts.note: N is the grammatical abbreviation for noun

explanation.surface: Someone works confusedly without using any nouns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside: the anagram ESPERATO goes round N.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an artificial international language devised by Zamenhof in 1887.

clue.text: Cat brought to water in French castle

parts.note: chat is the French word for cat
eau is the French word for water

explanation.surface: A cat is taken to the moat of a French castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' serves the definition and also tells you both pieces are French words.
explanation.definitionFit: A chateau is a French castle or large country house.

clue.text: Maybe Hearts and Hibs meet in unspeakable tragedy

definitions.meaning: Hearts and Hibs are Edinburgh football clubs, so a match between them is a play (a game) in Scotland
actors superstitiously avoid naming Macbeth in a theatre and use a euphemism instead

explanation.surface: An Edinburgh football derby ends in a disaster too awful to describe.
explanation.walkthrough: Heart of Midlothian and Hibernian are rival Scottish football clubs. In theatres it is thought unlucky to say Shakespeare's Macbeth aloud, so it is called by this euphemism.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatre folklore makes the title of Shakespeare's Scottish tragedy literally unsayable, so actors use this roundabout name.

clue.text: Fees schedule brings row over advertiser's margins

indicators.note: the row is placed over, covering, the pair of letters, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a tiff is a minor quarrel or row

indicators.note: the margins of a word are its outer letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A price list sparks a quarrel about how much space an advert takes at the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'margins' picks A and R from advertiser's; 'over' puts TIFF round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a published list of charges, such as a hotel's room rates or customs duties.

clue.text: Presidents honour service personnel

parts.note: CH is the Companion of Honour, a British order
airmen serve in the air force

explanation.surface: Heads of organisations pay tribute to members of the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: The person presiding over a board or meeting, a president, holds the chair.

clue.text: Structure in Steinbeck shows genius

indicators.note: the clue words show, or display, the answer within them, running across their joins

explanation.surface: The architecture of a Steinbeck novel reveals brilliance.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the last E of Structure, through 'in', into STEIN of Steinbeck.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein's name is used as a byword for any brilliant person.

clue.text: Tight cord flexed when first pulled

parts.note: string is a thin cord

indicators.note: pulling the first letter removes it from the start of the word

parts.note: flexed means bent

explanation.surface: A taut cord bent once it has first been tugged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when first pulled' takes B from BENT, leaving ENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stringent rules are strict and tight, with little latitude.

clue.text: Ridiculed arrangement trapping knight

indicators.note: one thing trapping another holds it inside, so the knight goes inside the arrangement

parts.note: a set-up is an arrangement or organisation
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight is mocked after falling into a scheme designed to catch him.
explanation.definitionFit: To send something up is to parody or mock it, so ridiculed is a near synonym.

clue.text: Sends copy to support hospital orderly

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits beneath the one it supports

parts.note: to ship goods is to send them
to ape is to copy

explanation.surface: Someone sends a duplicate to back up a hospital orderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'orderly' looks like a hospital worker, but it is the adjective for neat.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape means neat and in good order, as a well-kept ship should be.

clue.text: Split in spire damaged with load

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the combined letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crack appears in a church spire weakened by a heavy load.
explanation.definitionFit: A polarised opinion is divided into two opposing camps, so it is split.

clue.text: Nuts free to generate capital

parts.note: nuts means crazy, mad
to rid is to free of something

explanation.surface: Crazy schemes to make money for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but is the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Madrid is the capital city of Spain.

clue.text: Stop sailor heading out from Gdansk?

parts.note: AB is an able-bodied seaman

indicators.note: the heading, or first letter, is put out of the word

parts.note: Gdansk is a city in Poland, so something from there is Polish; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: A sailor is told to halt as he heads out of a Polish port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading out' takes P from POLISH, leaving OLISH.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish a law or practice is to put an end to it.

clue.text: Nightingale one left to occupy nest in place

indicators.note: the nest with its occupants sits within the abbreviation for place

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names

indicators.note: occupying a home means living inside it, so the one and left go within the nest

parts.note: a nest is a bird's home
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single nightingale stays behind to take over a nest somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested containers: 'to occupy' puts one and left in the nest, and 'in' puts that inside place.
explanation.definitionFit: Philomel is a poetic name for the songbird, from Philomela, who in Greek myth was turned into one.

clue.text: One frequently landed with large fishing bill

definitions.text: One frequently landed with large fishing bill

parts.words: One frequently landed with large fishing bill
parts.note: sounds like someone often stuck with a big bill for a fishing trip, but describes a water bird with a huge pouched beak that fishes and comes ashore

explanation.surface: Someone who often gets stuck paying a big bill for fishing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'landed with' means saddled with, but the bird literally lands; its bill is its beak.
explanation.definitionFit: The pelican is a large water bird noted for its enormous pouched beak, used for scooping fish.

clue.text: 8 sees old woman caught by Hebrew character

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, one's old woman
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
beth is the second letter of the Hebrew alphabet

explanation.surface: The answer to 8 sees a mother caught by a Hebrew letter.
explanation.walkthrough: '8' refers to the answer at 8 across, the euphemism for this play. 'caught by' only joins the charade pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Macbeth is the play actors refer to by the euphemism at 8.

clue.text: Old sailors with invitation going round duchy

indicators.note: the invitation surrounds the other letters, going round them

parts.note: a call is a summons or invitation
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Retired seamen are invited to visit an aristocrat's estate.
explanation.walkthrough: CORNWALL is a county in south-west England that is also a royal duchy, whose estates fund the heir to the throne.
explanation.definitionFit: The Duchy of Cornwall is a royal estate held by the monarch's eldest son.

clue.text: News provider concealed bug

parts.note: AP is the Associated Press news agency
concealed means hid

explanation.surface: A news agency hid a listening device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bug' suggests surveillance; it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: An aphid is a small sap-sucking insect, a greenfly being an example of a garden bug.

clue.text: Curse a barmy supporter taking cup

indicators.note: barmy means crazy, so the letters of the two words go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A mad football fan swears while holding up a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supporter' and 'cup' suggest a football fan with a trophy; the supporter holds a teacup.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucer is the small plate under a teacup, literally supporting it.

clue.text: Very rapidly appreciate those giving hand

parts.note: to appreciate is to like
giving someone a hand means applauding, so those doing it are clappers

explanation.surface: Applauding performers are thanked quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is British slang for at great speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A British idiom meaning extremely fast, from the clappers of a bell swinging furiously.

clue.text: Moved suddenly — photograph ruined

definitions.meaning: a snap taken with a camera
worn out, as in nerves that are completely wrecked

explanation.surface: Something lurched, the picture was spoiled.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means darted past, a camera snap, and, informally, worn out beyond repair.

clue.text: Infernal writer finally burned at stake

indicators.note: finally points to the end of the word burned, its last letter

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake put in before the deal

explanation.surface: A heretic writer finally burned at the stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at stake' suggests burning heretics; the stake is a poker bet.
explanation.definitionFit: Dante Alighieri wrote the Inferno, his journey through Hell, so he is the writer of the infernal.

clue.text: Female died in Slough

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
D is the abbreviation for died, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: A woman passed away in the Berkshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the English town in Berkshire, but here it is the verb to cast off.
explanation.definitionFit: A snake sloughs its skin, meaning it casts it off, a synonym.
